mapsettings.title: Map settings
mapsettings.intro: Changes the settings of this map in the project copy of its global.cfg: name and description in OMSI, the side traffic keeps to, how busy cars and passengers are, rail, years, money, tickets, seasons and the ground texture. Every setting shows the value the map has now. Everything you leave alone stays as it is.
mapsettings.curve.tooltip: Multiplies the map's daily curve by this factor; 1.00× leaves it as it is. Apply it again and it multiplies again.
@mapsettings.dropdown.current_mark: {name} is the name of a file the map uses now
mapsettings.note: Written to the project copy of global.cfg; the original map is not changed.
mapsettings.open.tooltip: Name, description, traffic side, traffic density, years, money, tickets, seasons and ground texture of this map
mapsettings.status.failed: The map settings could not be changed: {reason}
@mapsettings.status.failed: {reason} is a message of MapWorks in English
mapsettings.status.changed: Changed the settings of {name}. They go into the export of the map.
parklist.open.tooltip: Choose which parked cars fill the car park objects of this map.
parklist.title: Parking list
parklist.description: openOMSI fills every car park object of the map with a random car from this list, and leaves about a quarter empty. Tick the cars to use; a car that is already listed more than once keeps that weight. Only cars that have an AI car in the same folder can pull out and park in again.
parklist.empty: No parked cars found in the OMSI installation.
parklist.status.failed: The parking list could not be written: {reason}
parklist.status.changed: Parking list written with {count} car types.
parklist.status.unchanged: The parking list stays as it is.
parklist.number.tooltip: 0 is parklist_p.txt; n is parklist_p_n.txt, which car parks name with n as the first label of their object.
trafficcurves.open.tooltip: Set how much traffic and how many passengers there are at each hour of the day.
trafficcurves.title: Traffic curves
trafficcurves.description: How much AI traffic and how many passengers openOMSI makes at each hour, as a factor on the normal amount (1 is normal). Click or drag a handle to set an hour; the hours between are joined by straight lines.
trafficcurves.cars.tooltip: Density of the AI cars on the roads over the day.
trafficcurves.passengers.tooltip: Density of the passengers waiting at stops over the day.
trafficcurves.status.unchanged: The traffic curves stay as they are.
trafficcurves.status.failed: The traffic curves could not be written: {reason}
